The mode the graph was filtered for is asserted as fw:travelMode on the network entity -- the term reachability already uses for the mode it assumes -- from src/catchments.ts, so it is declared on the release whose definition is that module rather than here. changes.description: A downloaded or uploaded street network is kept in the browser's large store and the workflow keeps only a digest that points at it. Before this, the graph was written inside the workflow into a store holding 5,226,496 bytes, written twice on every save, so a network for a town-sized area could not be saved at all -- the download succeeded, the save was refused, and the graph was discarded. A graph is now written to the store BEFORE the workflow records the reference, so a saved workflow never reloads into a missing payload. Where the large store is unavailable or refuses a write, the widget says so above the Download button rather than leaving it to be discovered, because a fallback nobody is told about turns the larger ceiling back into the smaller one while the application goes on reporting that everything was saved.

A download is now made for walking or for driving, and the two are different graphs rather than different labels. Walking keeps footways, paths and steps and reads the one-way restrictions that apply on foot; driving keeps motorways and trunk roads, drops footways, paths and steps, honours vehicle one-ways and roundabouts, and reads motor_vehicle and motorcar restrictions. The highway exclusions follow OSMnx's drive filter so a graph here and a graph from OSMnx of the same area are comparable. The mode is part of the request, so a cached walking graph is never served to a driving download; it is saved with the graph, shown on the widget, and written into the receipt; and a widget further down the workflow that asks for a mode the graph cannot carry is refused instead of answered. Walking stays the default, so an existing workflow downloads what it always did.

Downloads are judged on what they cost rather than on how wide the area is: the fixed 6 km envelope is gone, and the byte and feature limits are their own numbers instead of following the isochrone graph limit. The default graph size is 50,000 network nodes, which admits a real town. Each instance's /api/status is read before downloading -- free slots, rate limit, and when the next slot frees -- and a busy service is waited for rather than treated as a failure. Responses are kept on the device and reused for the same query; pressing Download again when a network is already saved fetches a fresh one. The widget shows endpoint status before a download, progress on the button while it runs, which instance served the saved graph, and why a download failed.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

evidence.note: Acquisition only; the graph it produces is checked where it is used. The pacing follows the service's own /api/status rather than a client-side guess, measured against OSMnx's behaviour on 2026-10-19.
